svg.title: How to read the result: two separate tests, never mixed
svg.desc: A plain guide to the two tests in this proposal. Test A asks whether the whole map out-ranks the single pooled number and the missingness floor by at least 0.05. Test B asks whether the hot spots land where the biology says they should, checked by a fixed injection threshold of 0.60. The two tests are reported separately and never combined.
svg.text: Two separate tests, reported side by side
The proposal never mixes these. One asks if the map wins; the other asks if the hot spots land in the right place.

g.text: Test A: does the map WIN the contest?
measures separability only, no biology template
Score three readouts of the same mistakes by
how well they rank held-out abnormal videos:
pooled total (to beat)
full map (primary)
joint + time marginals
The map counts only if it beats BOTH:
the pooled total by at least +0.05, AND
the missingness floor by at least +0.05.
Test B: do hot spots land in the RIGHT place?
measures biology match, written down before results
Nudge one side's knee bend in the input, then
recompute the picture. Ask what share of the
new surprise lands in that side's knee and
ankle rows (4 of the 12 rows).
A blind spread would put only 4 / 12 = 0.333
of it there. We require at least 0.60, almost
double, before we trust the anatomy reading.
Below 0.60: the map is not tracking the body,
so no clinical reading of the picture is warranted.
Verdict A: is the SHAPE informative?
Clears both +0.05 margins: the layout carries
real structure the single total threw away.
Fails: signal lives in the total, not the shape.
Verdict B: does the shape match BIOLOGY?
At least 0.60 in the matched rows: the hot
spots track anatomy, as pre-registered.
A win in Test A never counts as a Test B win.

svg.text: Judged on whole held-out source videos; every number is transductive at the encoder. Folder labels are dataset annotations, not diagnoses.
